name: OpenCut
description: The open-source CapCut alternative. A free video editor for web, desktop, and mobile.
one_liner: A free, open-source video editor that runs in the browser, on desktop, and on mobile, aiming to replace CapCut, and it's being rebuilt with an AI-agent and plugin core.
buyer: Agencies and SaaS builders nervous about CapCut's pricing and privacy who want to embed or white-label a video editor they control.
business_use_cases: A social-media SaaS embeds the editor so users trim and caption clips without leaving the product.
An agency white-labels it as 'our branded editor' for clients instead of paying per-seat for a closed tool.
A course platform lets students edit lecture recordings right inside the site.

money_ideas.idea: Managed hosting of a branded editor for other apps, priced per seat or per render.
Build and sell premium plugins once the plugin architecture lands (transitions, AI captions, brand kits).

steal_this: The classic version works today. Host it, add one killer feature (auto-captions), and sell it to a single niche like podcasters clipping episodes.
